recipe_version.title: Maryland Crab Cakes with Old Bay Coleslaw and Lemon
recipe_version.description: Jumbo lump crab bound lightly with mayonnaise, egg, Dijon, Old Bay, parsley, and crushed saltines, chilled, then pan-fried until golden and crisp outside and barely held together inside. Served with a tangy Old Bay coleslaw and lemon wedges.

ingredients.name: jumbo lump crabmeat
ingredients.preparation: picked over for shell, kept in large lumps

ingredients.name: mayonnaise
ingredients.display_name: mayonnaise whose label lists canola or avocado oil, eggs, vinegar, and salt only

ingredients.name: lemons
ingredients.note: 1 juiced (1 tbsp for the cakes), 1 cut into wedges

ingredients.name: saltine crackers
ingredients.display_name: saltine crackers whose label lists wheat flour, oil, salt, and leavening only

steps.title: Mix the binder
steps.body: Juice one lemon. Whisk 1/3 cup mayonnaise, the egg, Dijon, 1 1/2 tsp Old Bay, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and the parsley in a large bowl. Crush the saltines finely and stir them in.

steps.title: Shape and chill
steps.body: Pick over the crab, keeping the lumps whole, and fold it gently into the binder. Shape into 8 loose cakes about 1 inch thick on a parchment-lined sheet pan and chill 30 minutes.

steps.title: Make the slaw
steps.body: While the cakes chill, shred the cabbage and grate the carrot. Toss with 1/3 cup mayonnaise, the cider vinegar, sugar, 1 tsp Old Bay, and the salt. Cut the second lemon into wedges (overlap stated).

steps.title: Pan-fry the cakes
steps.body: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium. Pan-fry 4 cakes until deep golden and crisp, about 4 minutes per side, turning once with a wide spatula. Repeat with the rest of the oil and cakes. Check one reads 165 F at the center.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Serve two crab cakes each with a heap of slaw and lemon wedges.

equipment: rimmed sheet pan lined with parchment
